newsitem.title: USA: Greenbrier says may see growth difficulties.
newsitem.headline: Greenbrier says may see growth difficulties.

text.p: Greenbrier Cos Inc said Thursday that 1997 will be a "more uncertain year" in which the company may see difficulties in sustaining the growth of previous years.

In a release Thursday, Greenbrier said that the overall demand for railcars is not expected to be as strong as 1996 and that the company continues to experience a "temporary decline" in intermodal markets.

Greenbrier Thursday reported net income of $4.4 million, or $0.31 per share, for the fourth quarter of 1996, compared to net income of $4.7 million, or $0.33 per share, for the fourth quarter of last year.
The company said that results were partly offset by start-up and consolidation costs related to the recently acquired transportation logistics business.
It added that weaker performance in its intermodal business, particularly trailers and containers, also affected results for the fourth quarter.
